Shri Dilip Singh Panwar, learned counsel for the appell  Shri Bhuwan Gautam, learned counsel for the respondent/
Heard on I.A. No.9567/2024 which is an application for hearing during vacation.
2. For the reasons mentioned in the application I.A. No.9567/2024 is allowed.

3. Also heard o n I.A. No.2795/2024, first application under Section 389 (1) of Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 for grant of bail and suspension of remaining jail sentence filed on behalf of appellant-Pappu.

4. Vide judgment and order dated 06.09.2023 passed in Sessions Trial No.311/2021 by the learned First Additional Sessions Judge, Biaora, District- Rajgarh the appellant stand convicted under Section 450 of the IPC and sentenced to undergo 3 years rigorous imprisonment with fine of Rs.500/- and under section 376 (D) of the IPC and sentenced to undergo 20 years of rigorous imprisonment with fine of Rs.5,000/- respectively with default stipulation.

entities.text: First Additional Sessions Judge, Biaora, District- Rajgarh
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 5. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that as per the prosecution story the prosecutrix has been gang raped by the appellant and other co- accused persons.
Learned counsel drew the attention of this Court towards Para-5, 11 and 19 of the statement of the prosecutrix and also referred FSL report i.e. Ex.P-25.
It is further submitted that DNA report is not available.
During the medical examination the prosecutrix was found pregnant.
She has 2 CRA-12425-2023 been allegedly gang raped by three persons but no injury marks has been found in the medical report.
She has admitted pre-enmity with the appellant in pargaraph 19 of her statement.
The appellant was on bail during the trial.
There is no possibility of early final hearing of this appeal therefore, counsel prays for suspension of the jail sentence of the appellant.

6. It is further submitted that the identically placed co-accused Purshottam has been granted benefit of suspension of jail sentence vide order dated 10.06.2024 in connected CRA No.12655/2023 and the case of present appellant is on same footing as of co-accused Purshottam.

sentences.text: 7. Per contra, learned counsel appearing on behalf of respondent/State opposes the application for suspension of sentence and referred paragraph 8 of the statement of the prosecutrix.
He has also referred the statement of Dr. Shailly Garg (P.W.-4) and paragraph 53 and 54 of the impugned judgement.
However, the factum of parity with co-accused Purshottam has not been controverted by the counsel for the State.

8. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
9.

Looking to the facts and circumstances of the case coupled with the fact that there are bleak chances of early conclusion of this criminal appeal, we deem it proper to suspend the remaining custodial sentence of the appellant.

10. Accordingly, I.A. No.2795/2024 is allowed and it is directed that subject to deposit of fine amount, if not already deposited and subject to furnishing personal bond by the appellant in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of learned trial Court, the execution of remaining custodial part of the sentence of the appellant shall remain suspended and he be released on bail, 3 CRA-12425-2023 till final disposal of this appeal.

11. The appellant, after being enlarged on bail, shall mark his presence before the Registry of this Court on 22.07.2024 and on all such subsequent dates, which are fixed by the Registry in this behalf.
Certified copy, as per rules.

(AMAR NATH (KESHARWANI)) (BINOD KUM  V. JUDGE V. J  Sourabh Pappu vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 13 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/192361979/
